issues.description: Tests pass a zero-amount, zero-puzzle-hash Addition as a sentinel to bypass __post_init__
issues.detail: The test diff replaces `additions=[]` with `Addition(amount=0, puzzle_hash=zeros)` to satisfy `len(self.additions) < 1`. That is value-as-flag: a meaningless tuple of bytes standing in for 'I had no additions'. The data no longer describes the world. Either keep additions optional in CreateSignedTransaction or model the absence explicitly; do not encode 'no additions' as a fake addition.

issues.description: CreateSignedTransaction now complects three distinct request shapes into one frozen record
issues.detail: Adding `extra_delta`, `tail_reveal`, `tail_solution`, and `puzzle_decorator` to CreateSignedTransaction collapses XCH-send, CAT-spend, and signed-tx-creation into one type whose valid field combinations are unstated. The class shape no longer describes what it is about; callers must know which subset is meaningful. A common builder function, or a small sum of explicit request values, would decompose this without losing the dedup win.

issues.description: cat_discrepancy_validation mutates a value into either None, a tuple, or an exception based on tri-state Nones
issues.detail: Three correlated optional fields are validated by membership in a set and decoded with `# type: ignore`. The function is doing the work of a proper value type: `CatDiscrepancy(delta:int, reveal:Program, solution:Program)` constructed once at the boundary. Then the property is just `self.cat_discrepancy`, no None-juggling, no ignores. The complecting here is parse-vs-validate intertwined with field access.

issues.description: get_wallet called purely for its side effect of raising is place-oriented programming with a comment
issues.detail: `# opportunity to raise` followed by a discarded call is using a lookup as a validation effect. The intent ('assert wallet of type X exists') is not in the name. A `validate_wallet_type(id, Wallet)` helper would say what it does and remove the dead-looking line that a future reader will delete.

issues.description: Round-tripping through json_serialize_for_transport to call an in-process function is incidental complexity
issues.detail: send_transaction and cat_spend build a typed CreateSignedTransaction, serialize it to JSON-for-transport, then hand it to a sibling method that will deserialize it. The value is already in hand; the transport step is a tool artifact, not part of the problem. Factor the shared core as a function over values and let both the RPC entry and the in-process callers use it directly.

issues.description: puzzle_decorator typed as list but only the first element is ever consumed downstream
issues.detail: The field is `list[ClawbackPuzzleDecoratorOverride] | None` and the comment admits only one is supported. A list-of-one is a value lying about its cardinality; later readers will write code for the other elements that silently does nothing. Make it `ClawbackPuzzleDecoratorOverride | None` until the plural case actually exists.

review.summary: The deduplication instinct is right, but the chosen shape complects three distinct request types into one CreateSignedTransaction and then routes in-process callers through a JSON serialize/deserialize trip to reach it. The cat_discrepancy tri-state validation is still parse-mixed-with-access; lifting it to a small value type would erase the type: ignores and the None-membership test. The test change that fabricates a zero-amount Addition to satisfy a non-empty invariant is the clearest signal that the new contract does not match the world it models. Decompose the shared core as a function over values; keep the request types describing what they actually are.
